trails.title: Discipline, Discipline
trails.description: Hastily written lines in a standard-issue notebook, as clear and powerful as the lieutenant who wrote them.

content.text:
Date of Record: September 20, 1990

Recorded By: Lieutenant Moldir

Subject: Admiral Igor's Recent Actions

This week, Admiral Igor addressed the conduct of three subordinates and implemented the following measures:

Captain L. Harris

Transgression: Ineffective leadership during training, resulting in subpar exercise performance.

Admiral Igor's Action: Issued a severe warning and reassigned from current position.

Sergeant K. Rodriguez

Transgression: Breach of military discipline, unauthorized absence from duty.

Admiral Igor's Action: Gave a severe reprimand and imposed three days of confinement.

Lieutenant J. Davis:

Transgression: Failure to complete assigned tasks within the designated timeframe.

Admiral Igor's Action: Issued a severe warning and assigned additional personnel to assist with the investigation.

The source of the leak has been identified as Stefen Garcia. Leaked content: Vacuum bomb explosion footage?

End of record.

Notes to self:

It is evident that the admiral's stringent measures are aimed at reinforcing military discipline. We must ensure that every officer and soldier adheres strictly to their duties and maintains a high level of readiness.

Some officers believe he has been excessively harsh recently—discuss this with them.

High command's perspective—arrange a meeting for the admiral.

Tracking target "K"—Texas, awaiting scout report.

trails.title: Small Town Tales
trails.description: Every town has its own story, some fit for prime time, others for filling slots.

content.text:
February 5th

Well, ain't that odd? Pierce came back early this morning, scared out of his mind. I had never seen the kid so freaked out. He sped through town and only slammed on the brakes when he got to the front door, as if something was chasing him. That nut almost ran over Marita's little bulldog!

Only God knows what he ran into.

February 15th

The birds were chirping the whole night long. I had never seen so many of them gathered together. Oh boy, they were so noisy; I barely slept a wink.

Ruth was scared, she thought it was some kind of omen. What a joke.

Those long-beaked birdies weren't afraid of shotguns, that's for sure. I fired a shot at them, but only a few got spooked enough to fly away.

Father Morgan suggested hiring a "bird control team"—if such a thing exists in the big city, that is. But I still think we should assemble all the gun users in the town and kill all those birds once and for all, rather than scare them off.

March 27th

Had a nightmare, a very vivid one, though I can't for the life of me remember what it was all about now.

Ruth woke up scared too; I comforted her. It was just a nightmare, nothing more.

March 30th

Pierce didn't come back from Houston, but the police sure did. They said Pierce's employer in Houston reported him missing, thinking he ran off with their money.

I wouldn't put it past that sly fox.

April 10th

All night long, the birds were making that racket again. When I pulled back the curtains in the morning, I thought I was still dreaming, but it was real. There were so many birds they were blocking out the sun.

It was like a waking nightmare.

April 12th

The birds scattered.

Everyone looked kind of strange. It had been ages since I saw Marita walking her dog, and Ruth started bawling over the most trivial things. It's unnerving.

April 17th

Johnny's back in town, looking like his soul got swallowed up by the devil. I saw him running, screaming like a madman, then he just collapsed on the lawn all of a sudden, crying and begging for something to spare him.

Father Morgan came, but he had this strange look about him.

I heard what Johnny was saying. He was mumbling on and on about a "motel."

May 13th

I talked to a realtor. Yeah, it's come to that—I'm finally thinking about moving.

Why? I don't know. I guess you could call it a ... gut feeling? Maybe my mind can be eased a bit somewhere new.

items.text: A man lies in the grass just outside of town. He's strumming a guitar and humming to himself.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Ah, this is the life. A warm, beautiful night, a cold drink, and no one but me and the stars in the sky. Eh, maybe I'll just lie here till morning.
It's a young Zeno soldier, his eyes hazy from intoxication. He raises his flask to the twinkling stars above.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: A good night with good drinks! I wish every day could be like this.
A dark figure looms over him, but in his blurred vision, he can't make out who it is.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Hey, buddy, you're blocking my view.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Huh? Are you stargazing?
The soldier blinks. He knows that voice.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Has anyone ever told you that you sound awfully like Lieutenant Lilya?

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: The rider of Red 38. Heard of her? No one can fly like her.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Of course.
The soldier concentrates, getting the figure's face a little more into focus.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Oh, my! You even look like her.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Keep playing dumb, and I'll show you what it's like to have her kick your ass.
The soldier's drunken eyes finally focus to see Lilya herself, a look of displeasure on her face.
He stumbles to his feet, dropping the flask in his hand on the way up.
He tries to salute, but almost falls flat on his face in the attempt.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Lieutenant Lilya! Airman First Class Andreas at your service!
Luckily, he manages to complete the wobbly salute.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Are you the warehouse guard?
She looks at the soldier doubtfully.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Yes, ma'am!
Few would so eagerly admit to the dereliction of their duties. In a way, he possesses exceptional courage.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: On your feet, soldier. My Red 38 is in your warehouse for maintenance, and I need you to remove the gravity ritual from it.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Gravity ritual?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: If you don't understand what I'm saying, go get someone who does. I need it today.
The soldier ponders, slowed by his inebriation. Just as Lilya is about to lose her patience, the soldier's eyes light up.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Oh, right, the gravity ritual!

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Yes, yes, I know! Please, come with me. I'll take you to the warehouse!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Are you certain you can undo the ritual?

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Yes, ma'am! They made sure I got the hang of it before they took off. Leave it to me!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Lead the way, soldier.
They stand side by side in the factory, the wooden crate before them.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Open it.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Oh, I remember this package.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: I thought it was some kind of joke, or someone with the same name as you sent the package. Who would've thought that you'd come to Texas yourself?
He rambles on. Lilya's patience is coming to an end.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hurry it up, soldier.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Open the crate. Now.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Ma'am, I know you want to do this quick, but ... *burp*

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: I haven't been authorized to undo this incantation.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: If you can't do it, find me someone who can. I won't say it a third time.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Truth be told, there's no one else to turn to. I'm the only one left.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: I was made an Airman First Class to do this job. I was still in training before this, you see.
He proudly pats his chest.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: The others were either transferred back to headquarters or just left.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: I don't know where they are now.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: But since they entrusted me with such an important task, I'm sure I have a bright future ahead of me.
Lilya's patience has officially run out.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You just said you aren't authorized, not that you don't have the ability, right?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I have two options for you.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: One, remove the ritual now.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Or, two, I beat your ass, and then you remove the ritual.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Well ...

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Choose. No more gibbering.
She readies her fist.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: I pick the second one.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Huh?
She is genuinely confused.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Haha. *burp* You see, I'm happy to get rid of the ritual for you, but I can't do it on my own initiative.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: I'm only an Airman First Class. I can't make decisions about this stuff.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: So, you have to beat me up to avoid future inquiries.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: One day, after I'm promoted, I'll be able to better assist you, ma'am!

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: I mean, you're the best pilot I've ever seen! I even made a scrapbook of the reports on your flights.
Before he can finish what he's saying, Lilya has already clocked him.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Alright, no screaming, soldier. Let's do this.
Each hit seems to clear his head a little more.
By the time his face is completely swollen, he has snapped back to reality.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Stop! Stop! This is plenty to prove my innocence!

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: I'll undo the ritual now.
He squats down and performs the necessary movements around the crate. There's a flash of light, and the crate opens.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Oof. You almost blinded me there.
She eagerly grabs the Red 38 and feels the familiar touch of the cold metal in her palm.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Thanks, soldier.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: There's one more thing.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Yes, ma'am!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Do you know why Zeno pulled out of here so suddenly?

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Hmm.
He squints, trying to remember.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: They said it was an order from "the top."

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: "The top"?

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: That's all I was told. But word is, it was because Admiral Igor got real mad about the video leak of the vacuum bomb.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: But that's just a rumor. Ever since the evacuation, strange things have started to happen.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Such as?

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: We started getting visitors from this group called the Order of Enlightenment.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: And now, the farmers have stopped tending their fields. The cattle and sheep have been abandoned in the wilderness. All the townsfolk do now is go to these gatherings, hoping that the Sufferer will bring them eternal joy.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: I don't know who this Sufferer is, but he ain't doing any good here.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Where do those people stay? In the town?

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Mm. It's a ways away, I think.
The soldier struggles to recall.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: A place called Tuesday's Motel.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Damn! Vertin! I have to go back!
She clasps the Red 38 with both hands, the cool grooves of the metal settling into her grasp.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Let's get out of here, girl!
With a victorious stance, she mounts the Red 38.
A silver light traces an arc in the sky as the pilot leaves the factory and disappears into the night.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Safe travels, ma'am!
The young soldier calls out after her, his voice soon swallowed by the night.
Short-distance flights are no challenge for Lilya.
She lands near the motel, guided by its glowing sign. The shadows of the trees around it look like hunched human figures.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Tuesday's Motel.
She locks onto her destination and is about to proceed when she feels something tap her on the shoulder from behind.
Hello, can you give me a ride?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I can't help you. Ask someone else.
Can you give me a ride?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I said I can't help you!
The repeated questions are getting on her nerves. She swivels around, ready to give the questioner a piece of her mind, but freezes on the spot.
There's a girl wearing an out-dated outfit. Her face has no discernible features, like it's been smoothed over with cement.
Oh, can I have some chocolate?
The faceless girl holds out a candy wrapper.
I met a kind man who gave me some chocolate. I've never tasted anything so sweet.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The hell—stay away from me!
Can I? Can I have that candy? More. I want more.
She opens her mouth wide, revealing a row of razorsharp teeth.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Stop asking me for candy. This isn't Halloween, idiot!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: *pant*

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Hey.
The pilot relaxes her poised fists when she recognizes the person in front of her.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: It's you.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Are you alright? You look pale.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You shouldn't sneak up on people like that. I could've hurt you.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: My apologies. But you're safe now that you're at the motel. No need to be frightened.
